I didn't seek help for almost a year because I was afraid that admitting drug use would end my medical career. That was a mistake. When I froze during my rotation, my supervisor suggested the confidential staff support service. That's how I found my therapist. We did trauma-focused CBT and later EMDR for the courtyard memory. EMDR has been the most helpful thing. The sound still comes, but it's quieter.

I visited M in rehab, and later we talked properly about that night. He told me he remembers nothing and that he's never thought for a second that I pushed him. Hearing it from him helped more than anything else, although the doubt still creeps in.

I stopped drinking for a year. I run a lot. I did a first aid instructor course, which sounds odd, but going through the scenarios again and again in a safe setting helped with the guilt about freezing.

I have a supervisor at work who knows the whole story and lets me swap out of certain cases when I need to.

I'm functioning well now, but I'm not over it.
Mit Freunden darüber geredet. Ich gehe wieder wandern, aber nur tagsüber. Ein paar Atemübungen gegen die Angst im Dunkeln.
Exposure on my own, walking barefoot on the lawn a bit at a time. My partner helped. I did not go back to the jungle.
Ich habe eine Psychotherapie begonnen, die mir hilft, die Trennung zu verarbeiten. Am Anfang habe ich auch Antidepressiva genommen. Es geht mir langsam besser.

I wrote to the influencer about what happened and got an automated reply about the 'integration bonus module'. That made me furious. I found a therapist who has experience with bullying trauma and psychedelic harms. We've been working together for over a year, mostly on my self-worth and on stopping the self-harm. My GP prescribed sertraline. I also joined a group for adults who were bullied as children. I'm better, but the voice is still there on bad days.

I've tried a lot. Neurologist (tests normal). Psychiatrist, who tried two SSRIs, which didn't change the DP, and later lamotrigine, which helped a little. A therapist who specialises in DP/DR, which was the most useful, she helped me stop fighting the episodes and stop monitoring my body all the time. I also took up a slower, more mindful style of dancing for a while, which helped me reconnect with my limbs. Avoiding bright, busy places helps but also limits my life. I'm still struggling with episodes every few weeks.
Complained to the hospital. Talked to friends. Slowly got over it.

Ich habe eine Traumatherapie angefangen, in der ich zum ersten Mal ausführlich über meine Kindheit spreche. Es ist schwer, aber es hilft. Mit meinem Bruder habe ich viel über diesen Abend und über früher geredet, was uns näher gebracht hat. Ich habe mich entschieden, meinen Vater vorerst nur selten zu sehen.
Kardiologe, der mich beruhigt hat. Danach wurde es von allein besser.
